blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: `enum Carrier { DHL("dhl", 499), UPS("ups", 549); ... Carrier(String code, long priceCents) {...} }` is used by a label service whose `switch (carrier)` statement has cases for DHL and UPS and a `default` that returns a generic template. A developer adds `GLS` to the list of constants, written as just `GLS`, and builds. What happens?

options.text: The build fails at GLS, since the constructor needs a code and a price and GLS passes neither
options.says: constant arguments are constructor arguments; a constant without them doesn't compile

options.text: The build succeeds and GLS gets null and 0, since an argument left out takes the field's default value
options.says: there are no default arguments; javac reports that the constructor can't be applied to no arguments

options.text: The build fails at the label switch, since the switch has no case for GLS and the compiler checks it
options.says: a switch with a default covers every constant, including new ones, so the compiler has nothing to report there

options.text: The build succeeds and the label switch throws for GLS, since the switch has no case for GLS at run time
options.says: the build fails at the constant; and had it compiled, the default would have returned the generic template

origin.section: A Constant's Data Goes Through the Constructor, So a New Constant Can't Leave It Out

questions.stem: `enum VatBand { REDUCED(7) { long tax(long net) { return net * percent / 100; } }, STANDARD(19) { long tax(long net) { return net * percent / 100; } }; private final int percent; VatBand(int percent) { this.percent = percent; } abstract long tax(long net); }`. What does `VatBand.REDUCED.tax(1_000)` give?

options.text: It gives 70, since each body reads the percent that its own constant was built with
options.says: a body is an anonymous subclass, which doesn't inherit the private field, so the code doesn't compile

options.text: It gives 0, since each body is created before the constructor has set the percent
options.says: the code doesn't compile; the body can't name the private field at all

options.text: It doesn't compile, since the bodies name a private field of the enum, which they don't inherit
options.says: javac: non-static variable percent cannot be referenced from a static context; package access or an accessor fixes it

options.text: It doesn't compile, since a constant that has a body may not also pass arguments to the constructor
options.says: a constant can pass constructor arguments and have a body, as CARD("CRD", 30, 290) { ... } does on the page

origin.section: An Abstract Method Makes Every Constant Write Its Own Rule

questions.stem: `enum Codec { FAST(1, data -> compress(data, level)), SMALL(9, data -> compress(data, level)); private final int level; private final UnaryOperator<byte[]> encoder; Codec(int level, UnaryOperator<byte[]> encoder) { this.level = level; this.encoder = encoder; } static byte[] compress(byte[] data, int level) {...} }`. What happens?

options.text: It compiles, and each lambda compresses at its own constant's level, 1 or 9
options.says: the arguments are evaluated before the constant exists, in a static context, so level can't be named there

options.text: It compiles, and both lambdas compress at level 0, the value before the constructor ran
options.says: the code doesn't compile, so no lambda runs at any level

options.text: It doesn't compile, since the lambdas name the field of a constant that doesn't exist yet
options.says: javac: non-static variable level cannot be referenced from a static context; a lambda argument can't see the constant it configures

options.text: It doesn't compile, since an enum constructor may not take a lambda as one of its arguments
options.says: a lambda is an ordinary constructor argument; only the reference to level is refused

origin.section: A Lambda Argument Fits a Formula; a Body Fits a Rule That Needs the Constant

questions.stem: `enum Region { EU_WEST("EU"), EU_CENTRAL("EU"), US_EAST("US"); private static final Map<String, Region> BY_CODE = new HashMap<>(); static { for (Region r : values()) BY_CODE.put(r.code, r); } ... static Region fromCode(String code) { return BY_CODE.get(code); } }`. What does `Region.fromCode("EU")` do?

options.text: It returns EU_WEST, since put leaves an entry alone when the map already has the key
options.says: put replaces the value; putIfAbsent is the one that keeps the first

options.text: It returns EU_CENTRAL, since put replaces an entry when the map already has the key
options.says: the later constant overwrites the earlier one without any error, which is why a collector that refuses duplicates is safer

options.text: It fails with an initialisation error, since put refuses a key that the map already has
options.says: HashMap.put accepts it; the duplicate check comes from a collector such as toUnmodifiableMap

options.text: It fails with an initialisation error, since two constants of one enum may not hold the same value
options.says: constants may hold equal field values; nothing checks them unless the index does

origin.section: Look a Constant Up by Its Code Through a Map Built After the Constants, and Let It Refuse Duplicates

concepts: An abstract method makes every constant supply a body, and a body can't name the enum's private fields.
Constant arguments are constructor arguments, so a constant added without them doesn't compile, while a switch with a default silently covers it.
A strategy passed as a lambda constructor argument is evaluated before the constant exists and can't see its fields; a body runs on the constant and can.
